requirements.requirement: The system must map raw phase value 'I' to a consumer-friendly label 'Phase I' and an explanation indicating early-stage safety testing.
The system must map raw phase value 'II' to a consumer-friendly label 'Phase II' and an explanation indicating initial effectiveness and safety evaluation.
The system must map raw phase value 'III' to a consumer-friendly label 'Phase III' and an explanation indicating large-scale effectiveness and comparison to standard treatments.
The system must map raw phase value 'IV' to a consumer-friendly label 'Phase IV' and an explanation indicating post-approval monitoring and long-term effects.
The system must normalize each phase value into a predefined score contribution consistent with the backend measure scale.
The system must output a structured object matching the UI contract defined in EVAL-CT-PHASE-UX-S1 including label, explanation, and score contribution fields.
The system must ensure that explanation text is plain-language and avoids clinical jargon beyond a general consumer reading level.
The system must handle lowercase or mixed-case inputs (e.g., 'i', 'Ii') and correctly normalize them to the appropriate phase mapping.
The system must return a default 'Unknown Phase' label with a neutral explanation and zero score contribution when the input phase value is not recognized.
The system must handle null or missing phase values by returning a fallback object with 'Phase not available' messaging and zero score contribution.
The system must ensure that score contribution values are bounded within the allowed range defined by the evaluation framework.
The system must produce deterministic outputs such that the same input phase value always results in the same label, explanation, and score contribution.
The system must complete phase interpretation processing within frontend performance thresholds (<=50ms per mapping operation).
The system must not alter or override backend-provided phase values beyond normalization for display purposes.
